title: Decidability of the nondeterministic tree-automaton index problem
formal: Given a nondeterministic parity automaton on infinite binary trees and a finite priority interval \(J\), is it decidable whether an equivalent nondeterministic automaton using only priorities in \(J\) exists?
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Define the parity convention, tree alphabet and equivalence semantics; transformations for deterministic or alternating automata do not settle this model.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence or universal proposition, or of its logical negation. context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Orna Kupferman. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: The index problem measures how much acceptance complexity is inherently needed to describe a tree language.

import_provenance.original_title: Decidability of the nondeterministic tree-automaton index problem
import_provenance.original_statement: Given a nondeterministic parity automaton on infinite binary trees and a finite priority interval J, decide whether an equivalent nondeterministic automaton using only priorities in J exists. This is an editorial continuation of Kupferman and Vardi’s work on transformations between acceptance conditions and tree-automaton emptiness.
